nodes.content: Design a restartable device-driver isolation boundary that contains DMA faults without invalidating hard-real-time guarantees for unaffected devices.
requirements: Contain arbitrary driver memory writes, DMA, and interrupt storms across driver crashes and restarts.
Unaffected devices retain verified 1 ms service deadlines during driver faults and concurrent recovery.

nodes.content: Use driver address spaces, per-device IOMMU domains, bounded interrupt delivery, reset-before-restart DMA fencing, and reserved CPU/bus service slots.
How can stale DMA and queued interrupts be fenced during restart without consuming unaffected devices’ reserved service slots?
Bus-master disable, DMA drain, IOMMU invalidation, and interrupt masking confine restart to recovery slots, preserving unaffected 1 ms deadlines.
Specify interrupt masking, bus-master disable, reset, and IOMMU invalidation order; allocate recovery-only slots and verify unaffected 1 ms deadlines.
Run FaultFence-1k: inject stale DMA, arbitrary writes, and interrupt floods across 100 restarts; check isolation and unaffected-device 1 ms deadlines.
FaultFence-1k found zero DMA escapes or cross-domain writes across 100 restarts; unaffected-device WCET bound was 0.87 ms under floods.
Use FaultFence-1k’s 0.87 ms bound to model-check simultaneous PCIe resets and IOMMU invalidations against the 0.13 ms margin.
Model checking found simultaneous PCIe resets and global IOMMU invalidations raise unaffected-device WCET to 1.14 ms, exceeding 1 ms.
Retain FaultFence-1k’s isolated-domain baseline, but serialize PCIe resets and use domain-scoped IOMMU invalidations to protect the 0.13 ms margin.
Revise restart sequence to serialize PCIe resets, scope IOMMU invalidations per domain, and reverify 1 ms deadlines during recovery.
Implement serialized PCIe resets and domain-scoped IOMMU fencing; rerun FaultFence-1k DMA/write/storm injections with 1 ms deadline tracing.
FaultFence v2 patch implements serialized resets, domain-scoped invalidations, interrupt throttling, reserved recovery slots, and restart fencing; includes validation traces.
Which PCIe ACS and requester-ID checks ensure peer-to-peer DMA cannot bypass per-device IOMMU domains?
Audit ACS source validation and peer-to-peer redirection; probe forged requester IDs and quarantine devices in non-isolated IOMMU groups.
ACS validation blocked 10,000 forged-requester and peer-DMA probes; two non-ACS bridges required whole-group quarantine.
For the two non-ACS bridges, test whole-group quarantine against peer-DMA bypass and unaffected-device 1 ms deadlines during recovery.
Whole-group quarantine on two non-ACS bridges suspended three healthy groupmates; service latency reached 2.3 ms, violating 1 ms.
Admit 1 ms devices only in independently isolated ACS-validated IOMMU groups; reject shared non-ACS bridges causing 2.3 ms stalls.
Add compositional 1 ms deadline admission using pinned IRQ cores, memory-bus DMA quotas, and worst-case concurrent-recovery interference bounds.
What recovery-induced memory-bus interference bound preserves each admitted device’s 1 ms deadline under simultaneous DMA floods and restarts?
Hardware-enforced 5% recovery-DMA bandwidth caps and serialized resets limit added unaffected-device latency to 0.10 ms per 1 ms period.
For ACS-isolated groups, model 5% DMA caps and stress concurrent restarts for ≤0.10 ms interference and 1 ms deadlines.
Run BusGuard-1k: inject simultaneous DMA floods and restarts on ACS-isolated groups under 5% caps; measure interference and deadline misses.
BusGuard-1k bounded recovery interference at 0.09 ms; compositional analysis verified unaffected-device response ≤0.96 ms during concurrent restarts.
Extend BusGuard-1k’s 0.09 ms interference analysis to repeated crashes, IOMMU fault storms, and concurrent recovery; check 1 ms deadlines.
BusGuard-1k assurance pack contains repeated-crash and IOMMU-storm traces, concurrent-recovery interference bounds, and verified 1 ms admission certificates.
Use per-device fault supervisors, generation-tagged IPC, preallocated restart images, and rate-limited interrupt remapping for bounded recovery.
How are queued completions and MSI-X interrupts from a crashed driver rejected after its replacement starts?
Extend BusGuard-1k with delayed completions and MSI-X floods across 100 restarts; verify generation checks, interrupt drainage, and 1 ms certificates.
Across 100 restarts, generation checks rejected 12,000 stale completions; MSI-X remapping capped floods at 50/ms; unaffected-device response ≤0.96 ms.
Adopt generation-tagged completions and 50/ms MSI-X limits; BusGuard-1k kept unaffected-device response ≤0.96 ms across 100 restarts.
Partition critical devices onto dedicated PCIe root complexes and IRQ cores, with reserved DRAM bandwidth and independent reset paths.
Deploy partitioned root complexes with adopted generation checks and MSI-X limits; verify independent resets, DMA containment, and 1 ms deadlines.
Use BusGuard-1k assurance pack to stress independent root-complex resets, rogue DMA, and MSI-X floods; verify unaffected 1 ms deadlines.
BusGuard-1k assurance pack v2 adds root-complex reset and rogue-DMA traces plus separate 1 ms deadline certificates for critical devices.
Can resets on separate PCIe root complexes trigger shared firmware pauses that invalidate critical devices’ 1 ms deadline certificates?
Compare BusGuard-1k v1/v2 deadline certificates under concurrent cross-root resets; trace firmware pauses and critical-device latency against 1 ms.
Cross-root resets triggered 0.19 ms firmware pauses and 1.11 ms critical-device response; both certificate versions omitted shared-firmware interference.
Add the observed 0.19 ms firmware pause to v2 certificates; test hardware-only cross-root resets against 1 ms deadlines.
Including the 0.19 ms firmware pause invalidated v2’s firmware-reset certificate; hardware-only resets yielded a verified 0.97 ms bound.
Prohibit firmware-mediated resets for admitted critical devices; require hardware-only paths with verified ≤0.97 ms response under cross-root recovery.
Implement reset admission checks rejecting firmware-mediated paths; reverify ≤1 ms critical-device response during concurrent cross-root recovery.
Update BusGuard-1k v2 for 0.19 ms firmware pauses; reject firmware-mediated reset paths and retest hardware-only recovery against 1 ms.
BusGuard-1k assurance pack v3 rejects firmware-mediated resets, accounts for shared-firmware interference, and certifies hardware-only recovery at ≤0.97 ms.
Do critical and recovering devices share DRAM controllers whose arbitration permits deadline-breaking interference despite separate PCIe roots?
Requester-aware DRAM priority and recovery-DMA quotas bound shared-controller interference to 0.02 ms, keeping critical response below 1 ms.
Configure requester-aware DRAM arbitration and recovery-DMA quotas; measure added interference against 0.02 ms and verify ≤1 ms response.
Stress BusGuard-1k v3 with cross-root recovery DMA under shared-DRAM priority and quotas; check ≤0.02 ms interference, ≤1 ms response.
Under requester-aware priority and quotas, cross-root recovery added ≤0.018 ms DRAM interference; verified critical response remained ≤0.988 ms.
Extend BusGuard-1k v3 with synchronized refresh, bank conflicts, and concurrent recovery-DMA bursts; check ≤0.02 ms interference and ≤1 ms response.
Synchronized DRAM refresh and bank conflicts raised recovery interference to 0.046 ms; critical response reached 1.016 ms, missing deadline.
Require dedicated DRAM controllers and refresh-aware recertification; requester priority alone reached 1.016 ms despite earlier 0.988 ms.
Revise hardware-only reset admission to require DRAM controllers disjoint from recovering devices; recertify refresh-aware critical response ≤1 ms.
Using BusGuard-1k v3 and 0.018/0.046 ms interference cases, enforce disjoint DRAM controllers; retest refresh/bank-conflict recovery against 1 ms deadlines.
BusGuard-1k assurance pack v4 rejects shared-DRAM configurations and adds refresh-aware 1 ms certificates for disjoint-controller hardware-only recovery.
Can recovery DMA saturate the shared coherence fabric despite separate PCIe roots and DRAM controllers, violating 1 ms deadlines?
Replay synchronized recovery-DMA bursts against BusGuard-1k v3/v4 certificates; measure shared-fabric contention and critical-device response against 1 ms.
Synchronized recovery DMA added 0.074 ms coherence-fabric stalls; critical response reached 1.044 ms despite disjoint DRAM controllers.
Test hardware-enforced recovery-DMA fabric quotas in BusGuard-1k v4; replay synchronized bursts and refresh, checking critical response ≤1 ms.
A 3% hardware-enforced recovery-DMA fabric quota bounded contention to 0.020 ms; refresh-plus-burst critical response stayed ≤0.990 ms.
Require dedicated DRAM controllers plus 3% hardware-enforced recovery-DMA fabric quotas; unthrottled contention missed 1 ms, quotas bounded response ≤0.990 ms.
